program_name: Forestry and Environmental Sciences (Scienze Forestali e Ambientali)
teaching_language: fully English - both curricula (Forests and Environment; Mediterranean Forestry and Natural Resources Management - MEDfOR) are completely taught in English
campus: Viterbo - Campus Riello, Polo didattica Agraria / Didactic Center for Agriculture (via San Camillo de Lellis) and Didactic Center for Sciences (Piazzale dell'Università), DIBAF (Dipartimento per la Innovazione nei sistemi Biologici, Agroalimentari e Forestali). MEDfOR curriculum: 1st year at University of Lisbon (Portugal), University of Lleida (Spain) or University of Padova (Italy); 2nd year at Tuscia (Viterbo).
academic_requirements: University undergraduate (Bachelor's) degree, or foreign equivalent recognized under current regulations, with at least 5 ECTS/CFU in each of: Chemistry (CHIM/03, CHIM/06), Plant biology/Botany (BIO/01-03), Silviculture (AGR/05). Foreign degrees/titles are assessed under an equivalence criterion by the Course Council (Consiglio di Corso di Studio), which also evaluates prior academic career and non-obsolescence of exams passed. The Italian didactic regulation (Art.4) additionally confirms the course is 'ad accesso libero' (open access) and that adequacy of preparation is checked via a written test ('prova scritta') on the same subject areas - see uncertainty_notes for the discrepancy with the English page's 'admission interview' wording. MEDfOR curriculum admission requirements/procedures are handled separately by the multi-university consortium (see http://www.medfor.eu/), not by UNITUS directly.
language_requirements: English CEFR B2. Accepted certificates/minimum scores: TOEFL > 87; IELTS > 5.5; City and Guilds (PITMAN) IESOL B2 communicator; Cambridge ESOL FCE; Trinity College London ISE II; British Institute ESOL B2. Other certificates may be assessed by the admission commission. Candidates lacking a certificate must take an additional English test as part of the Admission Interview. No Italian language requirement is stated for this fully-English programme.
entry_exam_or_test: Compulsory admission interview (per the English program page, for AY 2026-27) assessing individual preparation in: Forest Ecology and Silviculture (environmental factors affecting stand growth, forests and climate change, coppice silviculture, stand regeneration in canopy gaps), Forest Economy (market value estimation of small forest properties, stumpage value, forest ecosystem services), and Zoology (definition of biodiversity, eukaryota vs prokaryota, effects of invasive alien species). Conducted online (date and link sent by email invitation after document submission). Candidates without an English certificate also sit an additional English-language test during this interview. NOTE: the Italian didactic regulation PDF (Art.4 §3) instead describes this same assessment as a 'prova scritta' (written test) on the identical subject areas - see uncertainty_notes. No TOLC is required (TOLC applies only to restricted-enrolment Bachelor's programmes).
application_deadline_eu: No fixed programme-specific application deadline is published (rolling admission via interview). University-wide 2026/2027 enrolment window: opens 2026-08-01; standard deadline for Bachelor's and Master's-year-2+ students 2026-11-04; deadline for 1st-year Master's students (applies to newly admitted students on this course) 2026-12-29; extension for Jan/Feb 2027 graduates 2026-02-28. The program page separately states enrolment procedures (post-interview, post-admission) must be completed by a 'deadline November 2nd' with no year specified - this text is inconsistent with the confirmed 2026/2027 calendar (Dec 29 for 1st-year Master's) and appears to be leftover/unverified wording; treat 2026-12-29 as the operative deadline for AY 2026/2027.
application_deadline_non_eu: No fixed programme-specific application deadline; interview-based rolling admission. Additional extra-EU eligibility conditions apply (see academic_requirements/uncertainty_notes): born after 1997-12-31; not currently enrolled at University of Tuscia or any other Italian university; Bachelor's GPA higher than 28/30 (Italian scale, official MIUR formula); Bachelor's degree/qualification issued not before 2022. Eligible non-EU candidates apply via https://forms.gle/pV5Y7Xayv4WbwyRp6. University-wide non-EU calendar: onsite enrolment at International Students Desk opens 2026-08-01; consulate visa application cutoff 2026-11-30; Universitaly pre-enrolment portal opens for 2026/27 (typically April/May). Whether the age-limit/GPA/diploma-date extra-EU conditions are year-specific policy or a permanent rule is not stated on the page (see uncertainty_notes).
required_documents: EU/Italian-degree applicants (email route): degree certificate with full transcript of exams taken (PDF); short CV in Europass/EU format; English language certificate if available

Non-EU applicants (Google Form route https://forms.gle/pV5Y7Xayv4WbwyRp6): documentation proving eligibility (age, non-enrollment status, GPA, diploma date) plus the standard degree/transcript documents

University-wide baseline (for final enrolment, all international students): certified copy of secondary school diploma with Apostille/legalization and certified Italian translation OR CIMEA Statement of Verification; Bachelor's degree (at least 3 years) with same legalization options; Transcript of Records; Declaration of Value (consulate) OR CIMEA Statement of Comparability OR ARDI Statement of Correspondence; Diploma Supplement (can replace Declaration of Value if legalized); English certificate or EMI (English-Medium Instruction) proof; Admission letter
Proof of financial means for visa: EUR 10,179.85/year (non-EU students)

tuition_or_fees_link.note: ISEEUP income-based fee model; students not declaring ISEEUP pay a flat fee by home-country band (4 bands: EUR 600 / 1,050 / 1,500 / 1,950 per year per Annex 1 country list). Full regulation: https://www.unitus.it/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/TUITION-FEES-AND-CONTRIBUTIONS-REGULATIONS_2026-2027.pdf ; country bands: https://www.unitus.it/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/All.1_-Paesi_studenti-internazionali_2026_2027.pdf ; simulator: https://www.unitus.it/en/students/fees-and-contributions/tuition-fee-simulator/

source_quotes.quote: Il corso di laurea magistrale è ad accesso libero.

The adequacy of skills is assessed through an admission interview in accordance with the current Didactic Regulation for the master's degree courses. The interview aims to assess the students' individual knowledge in specific areas considered preparatory to the course: forest ecology and silviculture, forest economy, zoology.

L'adeguatezza della personale preparazione viene verificata mediante prova scritta con la finalità di valutare la preparazione individuale nelle aree di conoscenza specifiche ritenute propedeutiche per l'accesso al corso (Ecologia forestale, Economia forestale, Selvicoltura, Zoologia forestale).

TOEFL > 87; IELTS > 5.5; City and Guilds (PITMAN) > IESOL B2 communicator; Cambridge ESOL > FCE; Trinity College London > ISE II; British Institute > ESOL B2. Other language certificates could be assessed by the commission at the time of admission.
For the following steps, the student will be contacted by a tutor that will provide the support for the on-line procedures (deadline November 2nd).

born after December 31, 1997; are not current students at the University of Tuscia for First, Single or Second Cycle degree programmes or at any other Italian University; have obtained in the Bachelor's degree a Grade Point Average upper than a corresponding to 28/30 of the Italian grading system...; Hold a Bachelor's degree or post-secondary qualification issued by a foreign University or a recognized Higher Institution issued not before 2022

uncertainty_notes: 1) DISCREPANCY CONFIRMED: the English program page explicitly and repeatedly calls the admission assessment an 'admission interview' (for AY 2026-27, conducted online), while the official Italian didactic regulation PDF (Art.4 §3) calls the same assessment (same three subject areas verbatim) a 'prova scritta' (written test). Both are unitus.it/old.unitus.it primary sources. Could not resolve which format is actually administered in practice; both are reported here, with the English page treated as more current/authoritative for the day-to-day admission process description. 2) The 'deadline November 2nd' mentioned on the program page has no year attached and is inconsistent with the confirmed 2026/2027 university-wide calendar (1st-year Master's enrolment deadline is 2026-12-29 per the Tuition Fees Regulation 2026-2027); this looks like leftover text from a prior academic year that was not updated. Treat 2026-12-29 as the operative deadline and flag the page text as unreliable for this specific date. 3) It is not stated on the page whether the extra-EU-only eligibility conditions (age limit born after 1997-12-31, GPA >28/30, diploma not before 2022, no current enrolment at an Italian university) are permanent standing rules or reset/updated each academic year - could not confirm from a prior year's version of the page. 4) The MEDfOR curriculum's admission requirements and procedure are entirely delegated to the external multi-university consortium site medfor.eu, which is outside the unitus.it primary-source scope and was not independently verified in this pass; only UNITUS's own pointer to that page was confirmed. 5) No programme-specific official call/bando PDF exists (open-access + interview process, consistent with baseline); official_call_url therefore points to the didactic regulation PDF, hosted on old.unitus.it (legacy but valid UNITUS host).
